set_aside.subject: ProgressPhoto binary delivery failure
set_aside.text: “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as a storage error”
set_aside.question: What observable HTTP response constitutes the photo storage error, including status, media type, JSON error code/body, and whether it is distinguishable from other server failures?
options: A defined JSON error response with a specific status and stable error code
A generic internal-error response indistinguishable from unrelated server faults
set_aside.default_guess: Return a generic JSON 500 response with a stable concealed storage-error code.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer may read a visible ProgressPhoto, but its file_ref points to missing stored bytes.
events: The viewer requests the photo download.
The portal resolves authorization and then fails to obtain the bytes.
outcomes: The caller receives a defined JSON storage-error response with a stable status and code.
The caller receives a generic 500 response with no storage-specific contract.
witness.observer: The viewer client and its implementer

set_aside.subject: Failure-classification precedence for photos
set_aside.text: “An unknown, cross-project or hidden read is answered the same way … while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as a storage error”
set_aside.question: When a photo read is both unknown/cross-project/hidden and its stored content is missing, oversize, unlisted, or otherwise unreadable, which rule takes precedence, and must authorization and visibility be resolved before storage is inspected?
options: Unknown, cross-project, and hidden concealment always takes precedence; storage is inspected only after access is established
Any discovered storage failure takes precedence and produces the storage error
Precedence differs by unknown, cross-project, and hidden cases
set_aside.default_guess: Resolve existence, project access, and visibility first; return the concealed response for those failures without inspecting storage, and expose a storage error only for an otherwise authorized visible photo.

witness.initial: A viewer is authorized for project A. A hidden photo belonging to project A exists, and its stored file is missing.
events: The viewer requests that photo by id.
The portal evaluates visibility and attempts or does not attempt storage access.
outcomes: The hidden-read rule wins, so the response is indistinguishable from an unknown photo.
The missing-content rule wins, so the response is a storage error and reveals that a photo record exists.

set_aside.subject: Document storage failures outside the named cases
set_aside.text: “a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted, while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as a storage error”
set_aside.question: How must a document read fail for storage problems other than missing, oversize, or unlisted content, such as permission denial, directory/file-type mismatch, read I/O failure, corruption during reading, or a file disappearing after validation?
options: Every document storage or delivery failure uses the concealed response
Only missing, oversize, and unlisted use the concealed response; other storage failures return a storage error
Each storage-failure class has a separately specified outcome
set_aside.default_guess: Conceal all document storage and delivery failures to preserve the stated document policy.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer requests a visible ExpenseDocument whose path exists but cannot be opened because of a local storage permission or I/O error.
events: Opening or reading the stored bytes fails.
outcomes: The portal answers exactly like an unknown/cross-project/hidden document.
The portal returns a storage error because the failure is not one of the three enumerated document cases.
witness.observer: The viewer client and operations staff

set_aside.subject: Storage failure during streamed photo delivery
set_aside.text: “The portal streams that object through its own boundary” and “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as a storage error”
set_aside.question: If photo delivery fails after response headers or some bytes have already been sent, is partial output permitted, must the portal validate or buffer the complete object before committing the response, or is connection termination the defined storage-error outcome?
options: Validate or buffer enough before committing so the caller receives either the exact complete bytes or the defined storage error
Stream immediately and terminate the connection if a later read fails
Permit a partial binary response carrying some explicit failure indication if the transport allows it
set_aside.default_guess: Ensure readability and policy compliance before committing headers, then stream; if a later I/O failure still occurs, terminate the connection and record the storage failure.

witness.initial: A visible authorized ProgressPhoto is larger than one read buffer, and local storage fails midway through reading it.
events: The portal sends headers and the first bytes.
outcomes: The portal had validated or buffered delivery and instead returns the defined storage-error response without photo bytes.
The viewer receives a truncated photo followed by connection termination, despite the promise of exact stored bytes.
